# Funnel events

<!-- Rendered by `pnpm ops:posthog:docs` from apps/web/lib/analytics-registry.ts. Do not edit by hand. -->

One row per sender. "Named in" is the file, under `apps/web`, that writes the event name at its send. An event with sender "none" is one no source file names. A server event's own properties are listed; `captureServerEvent` (`lib/analytics-server.ts`) adds `account_id`, `internal`, `$process_person_profile` and `$geoip_disable` to what it sends.

## Distinct ids

- `browser`: the browser's PostHog id, which becomes the person's `users.id` once a signed-in page identifies the browser.
- `user`: the `users.id` of the human who acted.
- `owner`: the `users.id` of the account's owner.
- `visitor`: the signed-in human's `users.id`, else the browser's PostHog id from its consented cookie, else the fallback shown.
- `account`: the id shown, which names the account or the check, not a person.

## Consent gates

- `browser`: posthog-js capture, which sends nothing while capture is opted out.
- `request`: `serverCaptureAllowed` on the request's `Cookie` header (lib/consent.ts).
- `no_request`: a step, cron or webhook with no request: `serverCaptureAllowed` is given no cookie, so no visitor’s decision is read.

## Survey triggers

- `also`: a survey trigger, counted like any other event.
- `only`: a survey trigger and nothing else (ruling Q11): `pnpm --filter @crawlmouse/scripts exec vitest run ops/posthog/spec.test.ts` fails when an action, cohort or insight counts it.
